title: Reopening while the Close is held withdraws it with no reversal
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure AccountingHub is enabled for the organization and the test location has no QuickBooks Online connection.
  • Have a new Internal category for this test, category A, whose Account Mappings row is empty.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer, whose default internal category is category A.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed, with one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2, whose Close is Held for the empty row.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the Finance tab.
  3. Open the invoice menu on the Finance tab.
  4. Click "Reopen Work Order".
  5. Click Reopen Work Order in the window.
  6. Open Accounting > Accounting Events.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The document shows.

Step 3:

  • The menu offers "Reopen Work Order".

Step 4:

  • The window opens.

Step 5:

  • The status reads "Complete".

Step 6:

  • The Close shows the status Dismissed with the reason "Withdrawn: work order reopened".
  • No reversal is posted.
  • A Dismissed event offers no Retry.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11761 (Story 4, Reopen a closed internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11765 (Story 8, AccountingHub, the closed work order and its parts cost)

  • S4-E1: “If the Close entry is still held in AccountingHub, Reopen withdraws it instead of posting a reversal; the row stays on Accounting Events with the status Dismissed and the reason "Withdrawn: work order reopened" (nothing was posted, so nothing is reversed). In QuickBooks, Reopen reverses only what was posted at Close, to the same accounts (S7-R5): an entry posted to the mapped account or to ShopView Review gets its reversal; an entry never sent (S7-N5) gets none; an entry still waiting in QB Unexported gets none, and its row is marked "Withdrawn: work order reopened". An entry Marked as Exported by hand counts as posted (S7-E2).”
  • S8-E2: “If a work order is reopened while its Close event is Held, the Held event is withdrawn and no reversal is posted (Story 4, S4-E1).”
  • S4-R3: “Confirming reverses exactly the entries that were posted at Close (Stories 7 and 8), returns the parts to inventory as Reverse does today, removes the internal invoice, and sets the work order to Complete with its classification unchanged, the shop supplies amount kept, and the Convert and Change category actions offered again (S2-R9 applies only while closed or invoiced). The reversal is dated the reopen date, so it is held only if that date's period is closed or missing (S4-E2 is corrected accordingly). Events for one work order are processed in order, one at a time: a Reopen arriving while the Close is Held turns the Close Dismissed; a Dismissed event is never retried and cannot be replayed by hand; a new Close waits while an earlier reversal for the same work order is Held, shown as Held with the reason "Waiting for an earlier held entry of work order [n]", so two Close entries are never posted without the reversal between them. The reversal credits and debits exactly the accounts the Close used.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
